artifacts.notes: The PDF supplies the sermon entire, numbered sections 1-14, footnotes, and a modern source apparatus. It is stronger for Latin wording and source control than the Basilica's separate modern English web delivery, but its modern apparatus remains restricted and is not copied into the repository.
artifacts.rights_basis: Anthony's medieval Latin is public domain by age, but the PDF includes a modern critical and source apparatus updated in 2021 and the Centro Studi site displays no reuse license establishing permission to redistribute the complete file. The exact bytes are identified but not retained; consumers must paraphrase rather than reproduce the modern apparatus.

edition.notes: A complete fifteen-page delivery of the Twelfth-Sunday sermon. The Centro Studi page identifies these 2021 study files as an update to the Latin text and apparatus of the 1979 critical edition; this record does not claim an independent collation to manuscripts or the 1979 print volumes.
edition.publication: Centro Studi Antoniani, Fonti dei Sermones, digital study file updated by Valentino-Ireneo Strappazzon, 2021
edition.title: Dominica XII post Pentecosten — Latin text with critical and source apparatus

passages.context: Section 3 directly receives Mark 7:31 in allegorical and moral modes: Tyre is Judah or the world, Sidon apostolic hunting or penitential pursuit, Galilee Gentile conversion or penitential migration, and Decapolis the Decalogue; the section then introduces lust, avarice, and pride as the principal vices treated in the sermon.
passages.notes: Read in the exact Centro Studi Latin PDF with its local apparatus. The section is a medieval reception of Mark 7 and cannot establish the historical intention of the 1962 compilers or the architecture of the complete 1962 formulary. Paraphrase the modern delivery and apparatus unless a separately lawful checked transcription is supplied.

passages.context: Sections 8-14 sustain an exposition of Mark 7:32-35 through the heart and bodily senses, obedience and contemplation, confession and satisfaction, and the incarnate Word as healing hand. Christ's five fingers are applied to conception, nativity, preaching, miracles, and passion; saliva becomes the savor of wisdom; the sigh becomes compunction; and right speech coordinates confession with deed. Section 14 explicitly draws together the Gospel, 2 Corinthians 3:6, and the Introit's covenant petition.
